text: Dr. William Lee is a world-renowned
medical expert and researcher in
vascular biology and nutrition, a
pioneer in exploring the body's natural
defense mechanisms. Based on scientific
evidence, he has exposed the startling
truth about the harmful effects of
antibacterial mouthwash on our health.
First, this solution directly disrupts
the cardiovascular system's process of
producing nitric oxide. Nitric oxide is
a critical signaling molecule that
helps smooth muscles in the arteries
relax, dilating blood vessels and
lowering blood pressure. The body
produces this substance through a very
unique nitrate circulation cycle. When
humans consume nitrate-rich plants, the
body absorbs and actively pushes a
large amount of nitrates into the
salivary glands. However, humans cannot
convert nitrate into nitrite on their
own due to a lack of the nitrate
reductase enzyme. This vital task is
entrusted entirely to the symbiotic
bacterial population on the surface of
the tongue. When using mouthwash
containing antibacterial chemicals,
users inadvertently wipe out this
beneficial bacterial barrier. The loss
of this microbiome means neutralizing
the conversion enzyme, thereby cutting
off the reaction chain that produces
nitric oxide to protect blood vessel
walls. The second consequence is an
increase in blood pressure and a higher
risk of developing metabolic diseases.
A clinical trial on 19 healthy adults
showed that after just one week of
using mouthwash twice a day, their
systolic blood pressure rose by three
points. This figure is not an error
because it was measured using three
independent methods: clinic
measurements, home measurements, and
continuous monitoring. throughout 24
hours. In fact, this increase in blood
pressure appeared right after the very
first rinse and persisted for 6 days.
The picture is even worse when looking
at observational data from a study in
Puerto Rico on nearly 1,000 adults.
People who maintained the habit of
using mouthwash two or more times per
day had a 55%higher risk of developing
prediabetes or diabetes. In the same
group, the risk of developing high
blood pressure also skyrocketed to 85%.
The elimination of bacteria on the
tongue is the biological mechanism that
explains these alarming results. The
third consequence, which is aesthetic,
is the potential to cause very severe
tooth staining. A meta-analysis of 51
randomized trials confirms that
mouthwash does indeed reduce plaque.
But the price to pay is that using it
for four weeks or more leads to
extrinsic tooth staining, tartar
buildup, and taste disturbances. The
browning of teeth is not caused by
damage to the original tooth enamel
structure. This condition stems
directly from the antiseptic chemical
properties of the solution. It alters
the biofilm on the tooth surface,
turning it into a sponge that absorbs
dark pigments from coffee or wine. Most
notably, mouthwash does not completely
eliminate bacteria as advertised.
Research tracking hourly changes in the
microbiome has exposed a major paradox.
Mouthwash only reduces the bacterial
population tenfold during the first six
hours. However, between the sixth and
eighth hour, this bacterial population
rebounds extremely aggressively. This
massive recovery triggers an unusually
sharp spike in nitrate metabolic
activity. In reality, antiseptic
solutions do not permanently eliminate
the microbiome but only cause a
temporary collapse, followed by a rapid
recovery. Plaque is a biological film
that always regenerates as soon as
human intervention stops. Abusing daily
antiseptics turns the oral cavity into
a cycle of destruction and
reconstruction, disrupting the natural
microbiome instead of providing clean,
healthy teeth. Instead of destroying
the entire oral cavity with chemicals,
users should switch to a new care
routine aimed at protecting the natural
microbiome. The first and most
essential step is to use warm salt
water instead of commercial mouthwash.
This method requires mixing half a
teaspoon of high-quality salt in a
glass of warm water and rinsing
consistently for 30 seconds. Salt water
does not have antiseptic properties
that kill pathogens instantly, but it
can alter the local environment inside
the oral cavity. This solution creates
a natural osmotic pull, which, combined
with mechanical action, helps deep
clean between the teeth. More
importantly, salt water creates a mild
alkaline environment that completely
opposes the acidic biofilm secreted by
harmful bacteria. Studies on human
fibroblasts demonstrate that rinsing
with a 1%sodium chloride solution
strongly promotes cellular migration
associated with the healing process.
The biggest difference is that this
method does not destroy the valuable
nitrate-reducing bacteria on the tongue
surface. The second step in the process
is to use a stainless steel tongue
scraper instead of a toothbrush. Users
should pull from the back of the tongue
toward the front for 30 to 60 seconds.
This tool is incredibly effective, as
crossover trials show that specialized
tongue scraping cuts 75%of the volatile
sulfur compounds causing bad breath,
while toothbrushes only achieve 45%.
Medical data also indicates that people
who clean their tongues daily with
specialized tools maintain beneficial
bacteria groups that effectively
support lower blood pressure. The third
step is a strategy to control
cavity-causing bacteria by chewing gum
containing the sweetener xylitol.
Systematic data analysis shows that
xylitol acts as a biological trap for
the primary cavity-causing bacterial
strain, Streptococcus mutans. These
bacteria absorb xylitol but cannot
metabolize the compound, leading to
energy depletion and self-destruction.
The clinically proven most effective
dosage is 5 to 6 grams of xylitol per
day, divided into three doses after
meals. Consistency with xylitol reduces
dental plaque and new cavities. The
fourth step requires a radical change
in your brushing technique. Many people
today only scrub hard on the tooth
enamel surface while ignoring the
gumline where pathogens begin. The
medically standard technique requires
angling the bristles at 45 degrees
directly toward the gumline and
brushing with short, circular motions.
Are you making the mistake of scrubbing
horizontally, which wears down your
enamel? Leave a comment to confirm
right below. The final step to complete
the process is choosing truly safe
toothpaste and dental floss. Experts
recommend toothpaste containing
prebiotics to nourish good bacteria,
while completely eliminating the
foaming agent SLS and avoiding fluoride
, like the recommended Revitin product
line. The chemical SLS is a detergent
that creates thick foam in conventional
products. But double-blind studies
confirm that eliminating this substance
helps people prone to mouth ulcers
reduce sores and speed up recovery. At
the same time, cleaning between teeth
with microplastic-free dental floss
prevents toxic agents from entering the
bloodstream. A free, objective gauge to
verify the success of this routine is
to monitor your gum response. If you
strictly follow these care steps for
three consecutive weeks, bleeding while
brushing will completely cease. Beyond
physical cleaning, timing is key to the
survival of your microbiome and overall
health; the danger lies not just in
what you eat, but when you eat it. The
body has a perfectly natural defense
system: saliva. This secretion is not
just water; it contains antibacterial
proteins, minerals to repair enamel,
and acts as a continuous cleaning
system. During the day, the flow rate
of saliva remains stable at 0.3 to 0.4
ml per minute. Thanks to this, the oral
environment is always neutralized and
protected from acid attacks. However,
this defense system shuts down almost
entirely during the 8 hours we spend
asleep. The pH level in the mouth
begins to drop sharply the moment you
fall asleep and only recovers the next
morning. This means anything left on
your teeth remains there, undiluted,
and unneutralized throughout the long
night. The danger doesn't just come
from juice or ice cream; seemingly
harmless foods like crackers or chips
are the real silent enemies. All
refined starches are quickly broken
down into sugars right inside the oral
cavity. Even dried fruit, with its
sticky nature, clings tightly to tooth
enamel and dissolves very slowly. Even
the habit of sipping a glass of wine to
unwind in the evening causes serious
damage. Wine constantly recreates an
acidic environment, disrupting the
natural mineral recovery cycle.
Therefore, the unbreakable golden rule
is to stop consuming all food and
drinks at least 3 hours before sleep.
The last thing you put in your mouth
should always precede brushing to
protect your enamel from a long night
soaked in acid. The truth is that gum
health doesn't just stop at the oral
cavity but directly dictates systemic
conditions. The most shocking evidence
is the tight link between periodontitis
and type 2 diabetes. A 12-month
randomized trial was conducted on 264
patients with type 2 diabetes and
moderate to severe gum disease.
Astonishingly, after one year, the
group that received intensive gum
treatment saw a 0.6%reduction in actual
blood glucose levels. This level of
reduction has a medical value
equivalent to the effects of certain
specialized glucose-lowering
medications. Clearing pathogens from
the gums directly cuts systemic
inflammatory responses, helping
patients control blood sugar much more
easily. Furthermore, the reach of oral
bacteria extends as far as the central
nervous system, specifically regarding
cognitive decline. In 2019, the medical
community noted a breakthrough
discovery when specific gum disease
pathogens were found inside the brains
of Alzheimer's patients. Even more
terrifying, it is not just the bacteria
, but the toxic enzymes they secrete
that invade neurons, with levels
proportional to the primary agents of
brain atrophy. From this medical
hypothesis, a pharmaceutical company
invested in researching a drug
targeting gum bacteria to treat brain
atrophy in 643 patients. Although this
clinical trial was suspended by
regulators due to liver toxicity, the
connection between the brain and the
oral cavity is absolutely real.
Scientific evidence shows that chronic
gum infection is surely and silently
accelerating the process of
neurological aging. Maintaining a
naturally bacteria-free oral cavity
serves as a comprehensive shield
protecting the body, from the metabolic
system to the brain. The role of
magnesium and overall nutrition. The
big picture of oral health is not just
about the physical actions inside the
mouth but depends intimately on the
body's endogenous nutritional network.
In that complex network, the mineral
magnesium, also known as "maji," acts
as a decisive factor for the survival
of gums and the firmness of tooth roots
. A medical study analyzed in-depth
data from 4,290 adults and discovered a
surprising truth about the ratio of
magnesium to calcium present in the
blood. In people over the age of 40, a
higher ratio of magnesium compared to
calcium is directly linked to a
reduction in the depth of periodontal
pockets. These periodontal pockets are
essentially dangerous gaps that form
between the teeth and gums. They are
places where bacteria easily accumulate
, causing inflammation that destroys
soft tissue. Not stopping there, a
large-scale study that continuously
tracked 24,432 people over 5 years has
firmly reinforced this finding. Survey
results clearly indicate that those who
maintain high magnesium levels
consistently protect healthy connective
tissue and minimize the risk of
permanent tooth loss as the body ages.
This provides strong evidence proving
that magnesium acts as a crucial
material in building a solid foundation
for the entire tooth structure. However
, meeting the required intake of this
essential mineral is becoming a major
challenge for people in the modern era.
The best natural sources always come
from whole, unprocessed foods like dark
leafy greens, nutritious nuts, and
avocados rich in healthy fats. The
primary issue leading to widespread
deficiency is that modern agriculture
has almost completely depleted the
nutrient systems of our cultivated soil
. Today's fertile soil is no longer as
mineral-rich as it was 20 or 40 years
ago, causing a severe drop in the
actual micronutrient content of
vegetables. Have you ever wondered if
the plate of greens you eat every day
is actually void of minerals and

nutritional deficiency occurs so
silently, proactively using

For those with imperfect diets or busy
schedules, taking magnesium supplements
from rigorously tested brands like
Myoscience is an extremely quick way to
fill the gap. Furthermore, the process
of controlling gingival inflammation
cannot be separated from the ability to
maintain steady blood sugar and insulin
levels. A continuous increase in free
blood sugar acts as a toxic fuel that
stokes systemic inflammatory responses,
especially in sensitive areas like the
gum line. Therefore, the optimal
strategy to protect the body is to
prioritize foods rich in protein and
healthy fats while minimizing
nutrient-poor refined carbohydrates. In
mixed meals containing multiple food
groups, the golden rule is to eat
carbohydrates last, then take a light
10-minute walk so muscles can burn the
released sugar. This simple yet highly
effective physical activity will help
the body maintain absolute control over
the flow of excess energy. This
scientific habit plays a key role in
keeping insulin levels at their lowest,
thereby strengthening gum health and
the entire human immune system. End.
